props.description: Take a GitHub repository from nothing to an issue built by the build queue and merged by the merge queue, and know everything the pack writes.

text.insert: pack is a software factory made of five queues. You write an issue; intake triages it, the split queue files the issues a large item splits into when it can't be built as one, the build queue works it to a reviewed pull request, and the merge queue merges it. When a run reaches a decision it can't make, it pauses as one attention item for you to answer. This page sets that up on one GitHub repository, runs it by hand once, and then shows how to let it run on its own.

4. Write an issue the factory can build
The issue body is the contract every round is measured against. State the problem, why it is worth solving, why now, the desired outcome, the invariants, and acceptance; see

Run each queue once yourself before you automate anything, from your repository's checkout. Replace

You can also say what to build instead of giving a number, such as
archon workflow run archon-build-queue "build the retry fix" --detach
. An agent finds the issue you mean and claims it, asks you to choose when several match, or files new work as an issue and hands it to intake, which triages it before any queue builds it.

When a round ends on something the contract already answers, such as a review finding or red CI the change caused, the queue starts the next round at once as a new detached run, unless the fix would add machinery the issue does not ask for; then it asks you first. A pull request that changed nothing material since its last review, no commits or only cosmetic edits, never gets another round. The item is done when the pull request's latest review says Ready at its head (when only a check no round can run is left, such as a deferred operator check, the queue asks you for it once at that head), or when a maintainer answers
, for example after finishing the pull request by hand; the merge gate still checks the verdict and CI either way. Follow it with

One sweep agent decides every pull request the build queue made ready. It never pushes, never builds or tests, and never waits for CI. Each merge goes through a gate script that reads the pull request fresh and refuses unless:
the trusted review verdict says Ready for the current head (a push after the review voids it);
CI is green at that head;
the default branch's CI is not red (pending does not hold a merge);
the head contains the default branch, or GitHub reports it merges cleanly.
The gate merges pinned to that head through the forge's

Red CI in code the pull request doesn't touch gets one rerun of its failed jobs. If the default branch is red, nothing merges, and the queue raises one
; the forge can't rerun a commit with no pull request, so a flaky default branch is rerun by hand. A pull request it fails to read twice in a row is parked until the build queue readies it again.

The reason matters. A build or merge queue answer is written into the issue body as a dated "Current scope" section, and later rounds work from it. Every build item and merge pull-request item offers

7. Let it run on its own

The pack installs no trigger. Nothing starts until you start it, by hand as above or with a binding you add. A binding names the workflow, its inputs, the Archon user it runs as and how starts may overlap. The pack declares the bindings it recommends, and one command writes them as files for your repository:

archon trigger whoami   # prints the runAsUserId
archon pack bindings sdlc \
  --repo github.com/acme/widgets \
  --host build-host-1 \
  --run-as <runAsUserId> \
  --cwd ~/code/widgets \
  --out ~/.archon/triggers
is a name you choose for this machine, and
is the clone the runs launch in. The command writes one file per binding and prints what registers each. It registers and schedules nothing, and
run on a schedule. Fire each written file once, then install it. The command prints both lines for every file. Set
to the path it printed for each one; below it is the

BINDING=~/.archon/triggers/sdlc-acme-widgets-build-queue-0297fdfa94d5.json
archon trigger fire --config "$BINDING"
archon trigger schedule install --config "$BINDING"   # macOS
On Linux or Windows, run the same

command from cron, systemd or Task Scheduler.
If you already schedule a queue another way, remove that schedule first, or both start runs for the same queue.
